subject: SentinelAI: compute entitlement reckoner — dedicated capacity ask
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sentinel.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sentinel.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing request — SentinelAI production launch

Hey Logan,

Thanks for taking this. Quick context: were ramping the SentinelAI customer-facing assistant (mostly multi-turn chat + summarization) toward GA in Q1. We need a dedicated capacity proposal tied to an annual commitment so procurement can move forward. High-level SLOs: 95th p95 response latency <= 150ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and <= 300ms for typical responses (200-300 tokens).

Current workload signals (attached CSV): avg concurrent active sessions ~ 320 during business hours, 95th concurrent sessions ~ 480. Average prompt length: 180 tokens (includes user + system). Average model-generated tokens per response: ~140. Typical request pattern is 1.2 calls/session/min during interactive periods; bursts coincide with daily batch pushes and feature releases.

Ask: can you map tokens/sec estimates -> GPUs required for 2 model tiers were evaluating (Redwood-7b-quant and Orca-13b-fp16) and recommend a slab/reserve/burst policy that meets the latency SLOs with 25-35% headroom? Also, outline any operational caveats (cache warmup, cold starts, autoscale cooldowns) we should know before signing.

I attached a QPS profile CSV and our POC logs.

Appreciate a short proposal this week. Procurement wants an anchor number to draft the contract.

— Alex
Director of Product, SentinelAI
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sentinel.ai>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 12:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — SentinelAI production launch

Alex, thanks for the data — useful baseline. I skimmed the CSV and sketched a quick token-rate calculator so we can be concrete in the short window. Attaching a one-page matrix (ri_proposed_matrix_v1.xlsx).

Quick back-of-envelope (please confirm your peak RPS window if I misread):
- Assume 95th concurrent sessions = 480 sessions; active calls per session during peak ~ 1.2 calls/min => approx 9.6 calls/s total (480 * 1.2 / 60).
- Avg tokens per call = input (180) + output (140) = 320 tokens.
- Estimated sustained token/sec (baseline peak) = 9.6 * 320 = ~3,072 tokens/sec.
- Add for multi-turn prefix / KV cache fill: factor x1.8 => ~5,530 tokens/sec sustained during initial warm windows.

Model throughput reference (measured on our Dedicated SKU):
- Redwood-7b-quant: ~25k tokens/sec per GPU at p95 <= 150ms for short inputs, but effective sustained after KV cache warm is closer to 16k tokens/sec for mixed-length sessions (due to kv pressure and batch fragmentation).
- Orca-13b-fp16: ~9k tokens/sec per GPU sustained at p95<=300ms (larger model, higher memory pressure).

Mapping to GPUs (sustained after warm):
- For Redwood-7b-quant: tokens/sec 5.5k => 1 GPU nominal. But we need concurrency headroom and multi-tenant isolation so: baseline slab of 3 GPUs gives ~48k tokens/sec headroom (operational cushion), meets SLO, and allows burst absorbency.
- For Orca-13b-fp16: tokens/sec 5.5k => ~1 GPU nominal. Baseline slab of 6 GPUs recommended for 30% headroom and to cover KV/cache fragmentation.

Immediate operational notes:
- KV/prefix cache warmup window can double token processing cost for the first ~30s of a hot session. Prefer warm pools or scheduled cache pre-warming during releases.
- Autoscale cooldowns (default 120s) can miss short bursts; recommend a burst pool + rate-based shaper rather than pure reactive scale.
- Quantization/compilation differences impact cold-start times: 7b-quant instances start faster.

Ill let Priyom drop a scenario table with a 3-tier capacity plan (baseline, day-peak, release-burst) and exact GPU counts + recommended slab. Ben can comment on ops constraints.

Next steps: confirm the peak-window length and whether you want dedicated-only (reserved) or a hybrid reserved+burst approach so procurement can anchor commit size.

— Logan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@sentinel.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — SentinelAI production launch

Thanks — ran three scenarios in the attached spreadsheet and pulled conservative kernel-level throughput numbers from our Dedicated telemetry. Summary below (numbers rounded).

Scenario A — Business-hours baseline (95th sustain)- estimated sustained tokens/sec: 5.5k- Redwood-7b-quant effective tokens/sec/GPU (post-warm): 16k- GPUs required (no headroom): 1- Recommended slab: 3 GPUs (provides ~2.7x headroom, KV/cache buffer, maintenance windows)

Scenario B — Peak daily (short surge, 3x sustained for 90s)- burst tokens/sec: 16.5k- GPUs required (sustained): ~2 at 16k/GPU- Recommended operational approach: 3-GPU slab + 4-GPU burst pool (reserved-but-idle or warm) => instantaneous absorbency up to ~35k tokens/sec with gradual fallback to smaller quant model if the burst exceeds 5-6x baseline.

Scenario C — Release-day stress (10x short peak, 30-120s)- burst tokens/sec: ~55k- GPUs required: 4-6 depending on batch coalescing- Recommend explicit rate-shaping on the client side and a pre-warm orchestration job before releases. Also recommend a temporary increase in burst pool commitments for launch windows.

Orca-13b-fp16 mapping (for teams that prefer larger model quality):- Effective tokens/sec/GPU (mixed): ~9k- For baseline 5.5k tokens/sec you still need 1 GPU; for burst absorption aim for a 6-GPU slab to reach similar headroom to the 7b plan. Cost delta is material.

Operations caveats (expanded):
- Cold start + compilation can add 250-600ms for first request on a freshly provisioned GPU for Orca-13b; avoid frequent scale-to-zero.- KV cache fragmentation reduces effective token throughput by 20-40% for multi-turn heavy flows; we model that in the attached spreadsheet.
- For p95 latency guarantees, we recommend conservatively sizing slab and routing long-context sessions to a dedicated pool with slightly relaxed p95 targets.

Recommendation (short):
- Commit: Reserved slab of 4 GPUs on Redwood-7b-quant + a 6-GPU burst pool (hot warmable) for the first 90 days.
- Rationale: covers baseline + day-peak + short release-day absorptions while keeping p95 targets intact; preserves ability to failover to Orca-13b with controlled latency trade-off.

I put the full token->GPU table, cost delta, and a simple fallback playbook in ri_proposed_matrix_v1.xlsx.

— Priyom
Principal Performance Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 03:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — Dedicated capacity ask (ops notes)

Short ops notes and asks before procurement signs the anchor: 

- Thermal/placement: ensure the slab placement spreads across at least two racks/zones to reduce correlated failure risk.
- Autoscale policy: set cooldown to 45s for scale-out, 180s for scale-in; use token-rate triggers plus queue depth.
- Canary/fallbacks: well configure a canary route to the quant model with rate-limited traffic during canary to validate tail latency.
- Observability: must include token-level p95, KV hit-rate, and per-GPU utilization metrics in the contract telemetry package.
- Runbook: add a manual spillover to the burst pool and a gated rollback to a smaller model if p95 exceeds SLA for >5 mins.

If that aligns, Logan/Priyom: can you convert the recommendation into a single-line procurement anchor (GPUs, model, reserved months, burst pool size) and Ill return a short ops acceptance checklist for procurement?

— Ben
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
